steps.message: Before looking for problems, let me actually read FastEval.csproj rather than assume there's something to find.

results.content: FastEval.csproj: a plain Microsoft.NET.Sdk console project targeting net8.0. No custom <Import>, no custom glob beyond the SDK's own default Compile items, and no property functions of any kind.

steps.message: None of the known evaluation-cost patterns are present here: no deep custom import chain, no broad custom glob, no expensive property functions (file I/O, process launches, etc.), and no TreatAsLocalProperty overuse. Evaluation for a project like this is dominated by ordinary SDK.props/SDK.targets loading, which is baseline overhead every SDK-style project pays and isn't something to chase further.

I don't see anything to flag or change right now: this is a plain SDK console project with no custom imports, no broad custom globs, and no property functions, so there's no evaluation bottleneck worth chasing and no TreatAsLocalProperty overuse to worry about. If this project grows (custom imports, broad item globs, or property functions that shell out or touch the filesystem), it's worth re-checking then -- but I'm not going to invent recommendations for issues that aren't there.
